en: The
opposite of agentic engineering, so to say,
is the concept of vibe coding, which is
another crucial term you may have come
across.
The idea behind vibe coding is that you
build software without necessarily knowing
anything about software development and
definitely without caring about the details
of how the code is written, which
architecture is implemented, or which rules
are being followed. Instead, you only care
about the output and the results and not how
the underlying code looks.
It's the opposite of agentic engineering,
and unlike agentic engineering, it does not
require any knowledge about how software
would be built. The disadvantage of using a
vibe coding approach is that you can end up
with software that is quite messy under the
hood, that may break and may be hard to
debug. But of course, the advantage is that
it allows non-technical users to build
software and that you can focus entirely on
the output and the result without caring
about the underlying code. For complex
pieces of software, it therefore may not be
the right approach, but it's definitely
amazing for rapid prototyping or for
building software if you don't know how to
build software.
You just should be aware of the potential
disadvantages.
